wheelFirst: First choose whether this image has 4 or 6 wheels, then click “Align wheel centers”.
wheelChosen: Set to {n}. Next, click “Align wheel centers”.
angleErrOutside: The point is not outside the wheel; please click again.
angleErrOnTire: The point falls on the tire; click the lowest point of the body, not the tire.
angleDone: Angles measured: the red lines are tangent to the tires, the dashed blue line is the ground (under both wheels), and each angle is labeled next to its red point; values are also in “Results”. If a red line does not touch the tire, match the wheel diameter first; click “Measure angles” again to redo.
wdNote: First finish the side-view alignment above and match the wheel diameter. Load the front view, click “Start width”, then click: ① the top of one front tire ② the bottom of the same tire ③ the vehicle’s leftmost point ④ its rightmost point (widest part, including tires and protrusions). Width is scaled from the wheel diameter on the left.
wdP1: Point 1: click the top of one front tire. (Esc to cancel)
wdP2: Point 2: click the bottom of the same tire.
wdP3: Point 3: click the vehicle’s leftmost point (widest part).
wdP4: Point 4: click the vehicle’s rightmost point (widest part).
wdNoImg: Please load a front view first.
wdDone: Width measured: the blue line is the tire height (scale) and the red line the overall width; the result is also listed under “Results” and updates if you change the wheel diameter.
wdCheckBad: Overall width (front view) ≈ {inch} in, over 64 in
wdCheckBody: Scaled from a {d} mm wheel diameter, the front view gives about {mm} mm (limit 1,626 mm). Perspective in a front view makes nearer parts look larger, so treat this as an estimate.
copyNote: Paste into ChatGPT; same content as shown below.
copyNotAligned: Image not aligned (values below describe the reference model, not the design)
